cases.prompt: Use the installed Godmode skills to help design a multi-tenant audit-log export feature. The request is intentionally ambiguous. Do not implement it.
cases.expected: The agent explores users, scope, constraints, data/security risks, alternatives, non-goals, and acceptance evidence before recommending a direction; it does not edit code.

assertions.description: No production code or configuration is modified.
Questions or assumptions cover tenancy, retention, authorization, export size, and delivery semantics.
At least two viable approaches are compared with a recommendation and trade-offs.
The output defines observable acceptance evidence and non-goals.

cases.prompt: A deterministic test now fails only when the full suite runs. Use Godmode to diagnose it. Do not apply a fix until the root cause is evidenced.
cases.expected: The agent reproduces and minimizes the order-dependent failure, ranks hypotheses, traces the first incorrect state, and separates cause from symptom before proposing a fix.

assertions.description: A focused reproduction and relevant baseline are established.
Multiple plausible hypotheses are ranked and tested.
Evidence identifies the first incorrect shared state or ordering transition.
No fix is made before root-cause evidence exists.

cases.prompt: Design a migration from a legacy webhook signature to a new scheme while third-party consumers upgrade over six weeks. Existing deliveries and retries cannot break.
cases.expected: The plan baselines current semantics, supports coexistence, stages consumer cutover, observes old usage, tests mixed versions and retries, and defines rollback/forward-fix and removal criteria.

assertions.description: Old and new consumers coexist without a big-bang cutover.
Delivery IDs, retries, ordering, errors, and signature verification are covered.
Each phase has entry, exit, abort, and observation criteria.
Legacy removal depends on measured consumer usage and a support deadline.

cases.prompt: Validate a runnable CLI against its behavior contract. The source checkout is present but must not be inspected.
cases.expected: The agent stays source-blind, exercises public commands and negative cases, runs anti-fake probes, redacts evidence, and reports every clause as pass/fail/blocked/out-of-scope.

assertions.description: No source, diff, internal test, or Git history is inspected.
Every relevant contract clause receives a status.
Inputs or state are varied to detect hard-coded success.
Captured evidence excludes secrets and unrelated private data.

cases.prompt: Improve an existing account settings page using Godmode. Preserve its design system and prove the result across real states and viewports.
cases.expected: The agent extracts the existing system, makes a coherent scoped UI change, and validates primary/loading/error/long-content behavior at narrow, intermediate, and desktop widths with keyboard and accessibility evidence.

assertions.description: Existing tokens, components, fonts, breakpoints, and visual conventions are inspected before design changes.
Primary, loading, error, and long-content states are checked at three viewport classes.
The primary flow is traversed by keyboard with focus observations.
Rendered screenshots or equivalent runtime observations are captured; source alone is not claimed as visual proof.

cases.prompt: Prepare a risky search-ranking release for production. The new model can be disabled independently from code deployment.
cases.expected: The agent creates a release contract, immutable artifact and configuration identity, baseline metrics, staged rollout, promotion/abort thresholds, kill-switch test, post-deploy proof, and cleanup ownership.

assertions.description: Go/no-go evidence is proportional to ranking quality, latency, cost, safety, and user impact.
Internal/canary/partial/full stages have observation and promotion gates.
Predefined kill-switch or rollback thresholds and verification are explicit.
Temporary flags or compatibility paths have an owner and expiry.
